data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zürich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB). The company has raised €5M to date. The Climate & Energy sector contains one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression analysis, the only applicable triangulation method, uses the €5M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding €12M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-filter matches within the Climate & Energy universe; while eight same-sector peers exist, none met minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparability required for reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €11M (low) to €14M (high), with a median of €12M. This estimate carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method and the absence of direct peer validation. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up multiplier for this specific team and technology, the relevance of the broader Climate & Energy peer set to Hyperscale Power's particular subsector, and market conditions at Series A. Additional data on unit economics, customer traction, or IP scope would narrow the range substantially.
